h1: Telogen Effluvium: Why You Are Shedding, and When It Stops
subtitle: Sudden diffuse shedding, usually about three months after a trigger.

hero.alt: 200x scalp view of telogen effluvium with diffuse shedding, resting hairs and newly empty follicle openings spread evenly across the scalp
hero.caption: Uniform hairs, simply fewer, at 200x.

quickAnswer: Telogen effluvium is a shedding episode where an unusual number of follicles shift out of growth and into their resting phase at the same time. Those hairs release together roughly two to three months later, which is why the shedding rarely lines up with the event that caused it. Common triggers include illness or fever, surgery, rapid weight loss, low iron, thyroid changes, a new medication and periods of high stress. The shedding is diffuse across the whole scalp rather than patchy, and the follicles are not damaged. Most episodes settle within three to six months once the trigger is resolved. When shedding runs longer than six months, something is still active and worth finding. We read your scalp at 200x in Sandy Springs, serving all of Metro Atlanta.
takeaways: The shed shows up two to three months after the trigger.
Past six months, something is still driving it.

items.you: Hair everywhere, in the shower and on my pillow
items.why: Heavy daily shedding is commonly linked to a large group of follicles entering the resting phase at the same time, then releasing together.
items.check: We confirm the shedding is diffuse at 200x and look at what happened two to three months before it started.

items.you: It is thinner all over, not in one spot
items.why: All-over thinning without patches points toward a trigger inside the body rather than something happening in one area of the scalp.
items.check: We compare several areas of your scalp at 200x to confirm the pattern is diffuse.

items.you: The hairs have a little white bulb
items.why: A small pale bulb at the end means the hair shed from its resting phase. It came out at the root, which is typical for this kind of shedding.
items.check: We look at shed hairs to tell a resting-phase shed from breakage, which has a blunt or frayed tip and no bulb.

items.you: Something big happened a few months ago
items.us: Two to three month latency after trigger
items.why: Illness, surgery, rapid weight loss or a stressful stretch can push follicles into rest. The shed arrives two to three months later, which is why it rarely lines up with the event.
items.check: We walk back through the months before the shedding started, and check iron, thyroid and nutrient status in-house.

items.you: It has been shedding for over six months
items.why: When shedding runs past six months, something is usually still active, such as low iron, a thyroid change or an ongoing stressor.
items.check: We look for what is still driving it, and check whether pattern thinning is present alongside the shedding.

items.title: Illness, fever or surgery
items.text: A significant physical stress pushes a large group of follicles into resting phase at once. The shed arrives months later.

items.title: Iron and nutrient depletion
items.text: Low ferritin is one of the most common findings behind shedding that will not stop, and it is straightforward to test.

items.title: Thyroid changes
items.text: Both underactive and overactive thyroid disturb the cycle and produce diffuse shedding.

items.title: Rapid weight loss or restriction
items.text: Sharp calorie or protein restriction tells the body to deprioritize hair. The shed follows a couple of months behind.

items.title: New medications
items.text: Several common medications can trigger a shedding episode. Bring your list, and never stop a prescription on your own.

insight.kicker: What we see that others miss
insight.title: Even shedding, and follicles that are not damaged
paras: Even, all-over shedding points to a trigger inside the body rather than damage in one area. And because the follicles themselves are healthy, regrowth returns the same way it left: evenly.

faq.q: How long does telogen effluvium last?
faq.a: Most episodes settle within three to six months after the trigger resolves. Past six months of active shedding, something is still driving it and that is worth investigating.

faq.q: Why is it shedding now when nothing is wrong?
faq.a: The trigger usually happened two to three months earlier. By the time the hair releases, the illness, stress or change that caused it has often passed, which is why it feels random.
The follicles are not damaged in telogen effluvium, so once the trigger is resolved most episodes settle and density can return. Results not typical. Individual results will vary.

faq.q: Is losing 100 hairs a day normal?
faq.a: Daily counts are hard to read with textured hair, because shed hair collects in the style and arrives all at once on wash day. We account for how often you wash rather than counting hairs in a sink.

faq.q: Could this be pattern thinning instead?
faq.a: It can be both. At 200x, shedding leaves the remaining hairs uniform in thickness, while pattern thinning shows mixed thicknesses side by side. We check for both in the same visit.
